requirements: Every crate is fetched from the configured immutable registry, never through a cross-repository path dependency or Git branch.
Cargo.lock records the registry source and registry checksum for every crate.
The downloaded .crate SHA-256 equals the release manifest and core.lock.json value.
pnpm-lock.yaml records the immutable tarball URL and registry integrity.
The downloaded .tgz SHA-256 equals the release manifest and core.lock.json value.
Fetch the release manifest and detached signature first.
Verify the manifest signature with the separately pinned public-key fingerprint.
Fetch contract, Worker runtime, SBOM, license, and checksum files only from immutable versioned URLs.
Verify file byte length and SHA-256 before extraction or execution.

offlineEnterpriseMirror.rule: An Enterprise mirror may change only the download base URL. It must serve byte-identical artifacts, and core.lock.json retains the upstream version, commit, and SHA-256 values.

coreLockManifest.canonicalEncoding: UTF-8 JSON with recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, and one trailing newline
validationRulesBeyondSchema: The Cargo package names are exactly the eight consumableRustCrates names, without duplicates.
The npm package names are exactly @winwincode/contracts, @winwincode/strongflow, @winwincode/browser-ui, @winwincode/control-plane-client, and @winwincode/browser-core, without duplicates.
sourceTag equals core-v followed by core.version.
Every URI is immutable and every downloaded byte stream matches both bytes and sha256.
A lock update replaces the complete core object; mixed core versions are rejected.

upgradeOrder.action: Select one released Community core version whose manifest signature and source commit are approved.
Download the release manifest, signature, SBOM, license manifest, contract bundle, required Worker runtime bundles, Cargo packages, and npm packages into a temporary directory.

Verify the signing-key fingerprint, Ed25519 signature, byte lengths, SHA-256 values, one shared version, source tag, source commit, protocol version, SBOM, and license coverage before extracting or installing anything.
Replace the complete core object in core.lock.json in one change; do not combine artifacts from different core versions.
Update Cargo.toml and package.json to exact versions, then regenerate Cargo.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml from the approved registries.
Install with frozen locks, unpack the verified contract bundle, run schema and generated-contract checks, and reject drift rather than retaining an old protocol path.
Build the consumer Server and Web products, then run their PostgreSQL, identity, authorization, Worker protocol, restart, and product-boundary tests.
Commit the lock, dependency locks, generated outputs, and verification evidence together in the consumer repository, then release that product independently.

targetState.rollbackRule: Rollback selects the complete previously approved core.lock.json and corresponding product release. Runtime negotiation or dual support for old and new application contracts is not added.

firstReleaseGates.requirement: The release contains only the exact Rust crates, npm packages, schemas, samples, Worker runtime files, and supply-chain metadata listed in targetState.
All eight linkable crates package from a clean checkout, use registry-resolvable exact inter-core dependencies, and contain no path dependency outside their own package.
winwincode-session, winwincode-delivery, and winwincode-publication compile and test without rusqlite, winwincode-storage, or winwincode-postgres dependencies.
All three npm tarballs are built once, carry the exact core version, use exact inter-core dependencies, and pass package boundary and schema-to-package exactness tests.
pnpm contracts:check passes and the contract bundle contains exactly the five canonical schemas, two generated contract documents, and two protocol sample files.
Worker bundles for all four supported targets pass reproducible-build, helper-signature, ExecutionPort smoke, restart, and checksum verification.
The release manifest, detached signature, SHA256SUMS, CycloneDX SBOM, and component license manifest cover every released byte artifact.
Clean Cloud and Enterprise fixture repositories resolve only core.lock.json-pinned artifacts, build with frozen Cargo and pnpm locks, and contain no cross-repository path dependencies.
A release-content scan rejects Community UI, Server, Control Plane, SQLite or PostgreSQL product storage, Cloud SaaS features, Enterprise deployment features, credentials, and customer data.
